gen-megrim-gf-parkinsans: Futuristic and angular, Megrim draws every stroke at a measured, uniform thickness, while Parkinsans keeps its lowercase tall and its mouths wide. Crisp shapes are the strongest card here.
gen-megrim-gf-pathway-extreme: Pathway Extreme reads rounded and clear, with a big x-height. Its stubby ascenders and descenders keep long lines of text steady under Megrim's thin, angular headings.
gen-megrim-gf-preahvihear: Sharp, techy and a bit sci-fi up top, thanks to Megrim's uniform strokes with no tapering. Preahvihear answers below with a lofty x-height and mouths pried wide open, so the page feels both angular and easy to enter.
gen-megrim-gf-pt-sans-caption: PT Sans Caption reads big-bodied and inviting, its bowls left slightly unclosed. Megrim is best at angular, futuristic display lines where horizontals match verticals, and the body font is best at carrying the text.
gen-megrim-gf-puritan: Puritan brings rounded forms that stay open to the side, with oversized e and a counters that make the text friendly. And Megrim, built like bent tubing of one gauge, gives the headings an angular, futuristic edge above it.
gen-megrim-gf-questrial: Modern and a little stencil-cut, Questrial draws every stroke at a single weight, with short stalks above a tall band of letters. And if Megrim were made small, its angular futuristic lines would lose their presence.
gen-megrim-gf-radio-canada: Radio Canada stands its lowercase c, s and z tall and full, with a clear opening at the end of every curve. Megrim is best for angular display, while the body font simply carries the text.
gen-megrim-gf-radio-canada-big: Radio Canada Big reads with a monoline skeleton and terminals that finish well clear of the stem. Over many paragraphs, its x-height fills the line, and Megrim stays an angular, futuristic accent above.
gen-megrim-gf-readex-pro: Angular and futuristic, Megrim leads with uniform strokes, then Readex Pro settles in with broad gaps at the terminals. And its weight stays unvarying from word to word, so long text would flow smoothly.
gen-megrim-gf-roboto: Megrim is angular and futuristic, its joins as thick as its strokes, which makes it striking in display. Roboto does the quieter job, giving round letters generous mouths and a low contrast between capital and body height.
